title: ASSIGNMENT – 4
subtitle: Perceptron vs Multilayer Perceptron with Hyperparameter Tuning
name: Srikrishna O S

sections.heading: AIM
sections.paragraph: To implement and compare the performance of a single-layer Perceptron Learning Algorithm (PLA) without using libraries, and a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) with hidden layers and nonlinear activation functions. Students must select, tune, and justify hyperparameters such as learning rate, activation function, optimizer, batch size, and number of hidden layers.

plots.caption: MLP training loss curves across three experiments

rows: Built PerceptronFromScratch class with step activation and weight update rule
PLA trained on 62 classes using One-vs-Rest strategy; measured per-class accuracy
Trained three MLP configurations with different architectures (small/medium/deep) and activation/optimizer combos
Recorded accuracy and AUC for each; identified best-performing model
Tested learning rates, batch sizes, activation functions, and optimizers
Compared impact on convergence and final accuracy
Saved MLP and PLA loss plots for visual comparison
Loss curves show training dynamics and convergence behavior
Loaded 3,410 handwritten character images from Kaggle dataset
Normalized pixel values to [0,1], flattened 16x16 images into 256 features

sections.heading: LEARNING OUTCOMES
bullets: Implemented Perceptron Learning Algorithm from scratch, including the weight update rule and OvR strategy for multi-class
Built MLP models using sklearn, experimenting with different architectures, activation functions, and optimizers
Understood the impact of hyperparameter tuning on model convergence and classification accuracy
Compared linear (PLA) vs nonlinear (MLP) decision boundaries for handwritten character recognition
Generated and interpreted learning curves (loss vs. epochs) to diagnose training behavior
